name: Haughton impact structure, Devon Island (Nunavut)
why: ~23 km impact structure in a cold polar desert with permafrost, ground ice and impact breccias; NASA Haughton-Mars Project site since 1997 and Flashline Mars Arctic Research Station.

name: Atacama Desert hyperarid core, Yungay
why: Hyper-arid, high-UV, oxidizing nitrate/perchlorate soils at ~1 km elevation; Viking-style experiments on Yungay soils gave Mars-like results (Navarro-Gonzalez 2003). Coordinates = sample AT02-03A.

name: McMurdo Dry Valleys, University Valley (Antarctica)
why: Cold hyper-arid polar desert at ~1730 m where air never exceeds 0 C; dry permafrost over an ice table 0 to >70 cm deep; analog for Phoenix-site ground ice.

name: Rio Tinto headwaters, Pena de Hierro (Huelva, Spain)
why: Acidic (pH ~2.3) iron-sulfate river with jarosite, goethite and hematite comparable to Meridiani Planum; NASA/CAB MARTE subsurface drilling site.

name: Mauna Kea, Pu'u Hiwahine ISRU test site (Hawai'i)
why: Basaltic tephra cinder cone at ~2783 m used for NASA/CSA/DLR lunar ISRU field tests (RESOLVE, 2008/2010/2012) via PISCES.

name: HI-SEAS habitat, Mauna Loa (Hawai'i)
why: Barren basaltic lava slopes at ~2,500 m; long-duration isolated Mars habitat missions funded by NASA's Human Research Program (2013-2018). Same 0.5 deg cell as Mauna Kea test site.

name: Bockfjorden / Sverrefjell volcanic centre (Svalbard), AMASE
why: Arctic volcanic centre with carbonate globules analogous to Martian meteorite ALH84001, permafrost and glacial terrain; NASA/ESA AMASE instrument-testing expeditions.

name: Askja / Vikrahraun lava field (Iceland)
why: Young basaltic lava (Vikrahraun, 1961) and tephra plains in a sparsely vegetated highland; studied as a Mars analog for lava morphology and rover/remote-sensing tests.

name: Mars Desert Research Station, Hanksville (Utah)
why: Red Jurassic Morrison Formation mudstones with clays, concretions and inverted (exhumed) paleochannels; Mars Society habitat used for NASA-linked field research.

name: Death Valley, Badwater Basin (California)
why: Hyper-arid evaporite playa and alluvial fans; NPS documents NASA/JPL rover and Mars-mission testing in Death Valley. Named in the challenge text.

name: Lanzarote, Timanfaya volcanic field (Canary Islands)
why: Young barren basaltic lava fields and lava tubes; ESA PANGAEA astronaut planetary-geology training ground.

name: Pilbara, Dresser Formation, North Pole Dome (Western Australia)
why: ~3.48 Ga stromatolites and hydrothermal sediments, among Earth's oldest biosignatures; Mars 2020/ExoMars scientists trained here to recognise ancient life signs.

name: Erfoud, Tafilalt (Morocco), MARS2013 site
why: Northern Saharan hammada and dunes chosen by the Austrian Space Forum for the MARS2013 integrated Mars field simulation; also used for ESA/ExoMars testing.

name: Lonar crater (Maharashtra, India)
why: ~1.8 km young impact crater formed entirely in Deccan basalt, a rare analog for impacts into basaltic crust on the Moon and Mars.

name: Ladakh, Tso Kar basin (India)
why: Cold, arid, high-UV plateau at ~4.5 km with evaporites and hydrothermal springs (Puga nearby); used for Mars-analog and HABIT instrument studies.

name: Nordlinger Ries impact crater (Germany)
why: Complex impact crater with suevite and impact breccias; Apollo 14 crew geology training (August 1970).

name: Sudbury impact structure (Ontario, Canada)
why: 1.85 Ga impact structure with breccias and shatter cones; Apollo 16 and Apollo 17 crew geology training.

name: SP Mountain / Black Point lava flow (Arizona), Desert RATS
why: Barren basaltic lava flow and cinder terrain in the San Francisco Volcanic Field used for NASA Desert RATS lunar rover/EVA simulations (2008-2010). Coordinates = D-RATS SP Mountain site.

name: Cinder Lake crater field (Arizona)
why: Basaltic cinder plain where USGS blasted crater fields replicating the Apollo 11 landing area for astronaut training and rover tests (1967). Coordinates from NASA D-RATS guide.

name: Lava Beds National Monument (California)
why: Extensive basaltic lava-tube caves with ice and mineral deposits; NASA BRAILLE project tested cave-exploration robotics and biosignature detection. Covers the challenge's 'caves'.

name: Stillwater Complex (Montana)
why: Layered intrusion with anorthosite and norite; source rock for NASA's NU-LHT lunar highlands regolith simulant, i.e. a compositional analog of the south-polar highlands.

name: Negative control: Amazon rainforest near Manaus (Brazil)
why: Humid tropical rainforest and city edge: dense vegetation, very high rainfall and humidity, warm and stable temperatures; fails aridity, barrenness and thermal factors.

name: Negative control: Congo Basin rainforest, Salonga National Park (DR Congo)
why: Closed-canopy equatorial rainforest with high rainfall; maximally vegetated and humid.

name: Negative control: Singapore (humid tropical city)
why: Dense built-up humid tropical city at sea level; fails the built-up hard filter and aridity/barrenness.

name: Negative control: Kolkata (humid tropical megacity, India)
why: Monsoon-humid, low-lying, densely built megacity on the Ganges delta; no barren terrain, ice or low pressure.

name: Negative control: Sundarbans mangrove wetland (India/Bangladesh)
why: Ocean-adjacent tidal mangrove forest and wetland: waterlogged, vegetated, humid, sea level.

name: Negative control: Everglades wetland (Florida)
why: Subtropical freshwater/coastal wetland with standing water and dense vegetation.

name: Negative control: US Corn Belt cropland near Ames (Iowa)
why: Intensively cultivated temperate cropland on deep fertile soils; vegetated, humid-continental climate.

name: Negative control: Punjab irrigated cropland near Ludhiana (India)
why: Irrigated wheat/rice farmland on alluvial plains; vegetated, cultivated and built-up.

name: Negative control: Black Forest temperate forest (Germany)
why: Humid temperate mountain forest; dense vegetation, moderate temperatures, high precipitation.

name: Negative control: Hoh temperate rainforest (Washington)
why: Temperate rainforest with among the highest rainfall in the contiguous US; moss-covered, fully vegetated.

name: Negative control: NEEMO Aquarius Reef Base (Florida Keys)
why: Operations-only analog (isolation, EVA ops, comms delay) 19 m underwater; no surface-environment similarity, and it is ocean, not land. Should score low on environment.
